title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Salta and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the grape, Salta or Calchaquí Valleys, and often Cafayate and the vineyard's altitude. Many producers print altitude prominently, as it's central to the style. Argentina's 85% rule for named grapes applies.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Torrontés suits Salta's empanadas salteñas, small, juicy beef pastries, as well as spicy food, ceviche, Thai and Indian dishes. Salta's reds suit grilled meat, goat, llama and humita, a corn dish. Serve Torrontés at 7 to 10 degrees, young; reds at 16 to 18.

steps.prompt: Which dish is a classic with Torrontés in Salta?

steps.body: Torrontés is best young, within one or two years, while its floral perfume is fresh.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show grape, valley and altitude
Torrontés suits empanadas and spicy food
